bore verb

make a hole with a drill

also drill a hole, bore a hole, drill, drill (verb)

classical

Cato Agr. 41.3 (Lewis & Short)
Verg. A. 2.38 (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 165
Traupman 307

1terebrō: short e in the second syllable (Lewis & Short terēbrō, marked common). The vowel is short; the syllable is heavy only by position before br. Verg. A. 2.38, aut terebrāre cavās uterī et temptāre latebrās: the first foot, aut tere-, is a dactyl, so the second syllable is light.

terebrō1, terebrāre, terebrāvī, terebrātum

verb, first conjugation, transitive · Conjugation on Wiktionary

bore, drill

From terebra, the auger (see drill).

Other words

  • perforō, perforāre, perforāvī, perforātum — pierce, bore through

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Lewis & Short s.v. terebrō: syn. perforō · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    To make a hole right through.

Examples

  • terebrā vītem pertunditō

    bore through the vine with an augerCato Agr. 41.3 (Lewis & Short)

See also drill, electric drill.
